cert.ca_file_hint: Optionally attach the issuing CA so terminals can download and trust the root certificate; export only, not used for signing
cert.ca_import_hint: Imported CAs go to the imported-CA pool (the site root CA is not overwritten) and can be selected in the "Issuing CA" dropdown when generating certificates. CA private keys stay on the server and are never downloadable
cert.ca_generate_hint: A new root CA will overwrite the existing one; certificates previously issued by the old CA will no longer chain
cert.ca_help_title: How to trust the site root CA
cert.ca_help_windows: Windows: run "certutil -addstore -f Root foims-root-ca.crt" as administrator, or double-click the downloaded .crt file and import into Trusted Root Certification Authorities. Chrome/Edge/Firefox trust it after a browser restart.
cert.ca_help_linux: Debian/Ubuntu: sudo cp foims-root-ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ && sudo update-ca-certificates; RHEL/Fedora: sudo cp foims-root-ca.crt /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ && sudo update-ca-trust extract (PEM with .crt extension required).
cert.ca_help_chrome: Linux Chrome/Chromium does not read the system trust store; additionally run: certutil -d sql:$HOME/.pki/nssdb -A -t "C,," -n "FOIMS-RootCA" -i foims-root-ca.crt (requires libnss3-tools/nss-tools).
cert.ca_help_firefox: Linux Firefox uses its own certificate store: import manually under Settings > Privacy & Security > Certificates > View Certificates, or configure the p11-kit trust module via enterprise policy.
cert.ca_help_note: Import the root CA (not the site certificate); certificates must contain SAN entries. With a private CA, Chrome does not use local trust anchors for HTTP/3 (QUIC) and falls back to TCP automatically - expected behavior.
cert.ca_select_hint: Certificates are always issued by the selected CA (site root CA or an imported CA); generate or import a CA first
